newsitem.title: FRANCE: Three Corsicans held after bomb attacks.
newsitem.headline: Three Corsicans held after bomb attacks.

text.p: Three alleged Corsican separatist guerrillas were ordered held in preventive custody on Saturday on suspicion of planting bombs in a southern French town, justice sources said.
They said Anthony Galliot, Pierre-Paul Mattei and Antoine Lutzu were suspected of taking part in bombing the law courts and main post office in Aix-en-Provence in September and November.
The FLNC - "Historic Wing", a leading separatist group on the French Mediterranean island, claimed responsibility for both blasts, which caused extensive damage but no injuries.
Paris anti-terrorism Judge Jean-Francois Ricard placed the three under investigation for conspiracy with a terrorist aim.
Three other suspects were due to be presented to the judge on Sunday, the justice sources said.
Investigators said the FLNC faction used the men to set off bombs in its name, perhaps for payment. Several of them had large sums of cash when they were detained last week.
The FLNC exploded 76 small devices in Corsica last Sunday in a show of strength in response to a police crackdown. No one was injured in the coordinated pre-dawn blitz.
